HOW IT WORKS

  • Public identifier: lowercase hex SHA-256 of the trimmed API key, in the browser.
  • HKDF-SHA-256 derives separate AES-256-GCM and storage-authentication secrets directly from the ORIGINAL API key with different purpose labels. The public identifier cannot derive the encryption key. Provider labels separate vaults.
  • Every completed exchange is encrypted with a fresh random 12-byte nonce and authenticated with its provider, identifier, and unique exchange ID.
  • The PHP endpoint receives only the hash identifier, an independent derived access token, encrypted envelopes, and metadata. Never the original API key, the encryption key, or conversation plaintext. The original key goes directly to the AI provider, as it did before.
  • A public identifier without the derived access token cannot locate the vault. The server hashes both into a storage namespace; it never stores the bearer token itself. All calls require HTTPS and the endpoint grants no CORS access.
  • Writes append independently, so concurrent devices do not overwrite history. Retried saves are idempotent. Reads show the newest 50 exchanges; Load older conversations retrieves earlier pages. All saved entries remain until storage limits are reached. Storage defaults: 16 MiB per vault, 128 MiB total plus SQLite overhead; 120 requests/minute per IP. The quota failure never deletes history.
  • API keys, derived encryption keys, and plaintext are kept in tab memory only. No localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies, or third-party analytics.
  • The checkbox preference is not remembered; opt in on each visit. Enabling or disabling memory starts a fresh context. Earlier unsaved chat is not uploaded retroactively. Changing the key or provider clears loaded memory from the tab.
  • Only completed non-transient exchanges are saved. Partial/failed responses, speech, internal tool logs, and intermediate document chunk notes are not saved. Supplied passage text is included in a completed exchange, capped with its question at 28,000 characters; answers are capped at 28,000 characters. This matches the existing recent-conversation context limits.
  • Recent decrypted history is sent directly to the selected AI provider with new questions. Persistent memory is NOT a promise to hide prompts from that provider. Server metadata includes hashed vault identity, order, sizes, and short-lived hashed-IP rate counters; hosting access logs may retain IPs/times.
  • Unchecking stops future memory requests/saves. It does not delete saved data. Forget key removes the key and loaded memory from this tab, not the server.
  • Shared API keys share memories. Rotating/losing a key changes/loses access. No key migration or recovery feature is included in this first version. Keep the old key if you need old memory (revocation at the provider does not prevent local key derivation). A weak/custom key is unsuitable for this scheme.
  • A site administrator cannot decrypt database files using the stored identifier or bearer secret. Someone controlling the site can change its JavaScript to intercept a key on a future visit. This implementation does not prevent that.
  • The notebook download remains a user-requested PLAINTEXT export of the session's logs. Restored history is shown in the separate Previous conversations panel.
